minutes.headline: Sewer Commission credited a leak-hit resident, started a Tilton Ave service-area review, and left legal costs unresolved.
minutes.summary: The commission approved a sewer credit for a resident with a confirmed leak and voted to study whether the Tilton Ave area belongs in the sewer service area. With the town accountant and business manager present, it debated how to pay for town counsel, OPEB funding, indirect costs, and FY19 budget line items without finishing the budget. It also approved several sets of prior minutes and scheduled further budget work ahead of the Finance Committee presentation.

public_comment.topic: Resident of Tilton Ave asked to revisit removal of the street from the sewer service area because her septic system is failing and a private extension would be costly.
Resident requested a sewer credit after a water leak raised her usage and questioned how sewer is billed without metering.
A commissioner read a statement about a prior special-meeting call, claims about a supplier and engineer found untrue, and inconsistent data from two engineering firms.

votes.motion: Approve the potential sewer credit calculated by the business manager under policy for the resident with the leak.
Look at the Tilton Ave area and see whether it qualifies for the sewer service area.
Accept the office space charge for this year and have a subcommittee investigate for future years.
Send the restitution agreement draft to Dan for his signature.
Assess the privilege fee for the connection.

budget_items.topic: Leak credit for resident sewer bills
budget_items.what_was_said: Credit based on averaging four quarterly bills down to the historic average per policy.
Debate over whether the sewer pays legal directly from the enterprise fund or through indirect costs, with a fixed town retainer; any direct payment would need to be deducted from the town charge.
The accountant gave the sewer share of the OPEB liability and annual cost, and the commission discussed funding at the town's lower proportion.

129 thousand four hundred and eighty one dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: Sewer pays a flat amount for DPW office space mirroring other tenants; a member wanted it based on actual cost.

budget_items.topic: Liability insurance allocation for pump stations
budget_items.what_was_said: Sewer share is a percentage of town insured value; members questioned whether pump station values reflect replacement cost.
Members agreed to raise the engineering services placeholder for capital, service area and maintenance planning studies.
Debate over whether the sewer should buy or own meters and readers; a placeholder amount was discussed, with a member wanting revenue offsets.
A suggestion to lower the placeholder because this year's budget can cover upfront development.
Suggestion to spend more this year and reduce the next-year line, with a concern about rushing.
Budget includes a Fitchburg increase and Leominster increase; usage-based projection was recalculated.
A transfer to capital reserve was discussed and left unresolved, with the bottom line left in deficit.
The parts list rose since the earlier review and its funding source was to be presented.
The cost allocation came in much higher than expected and the commission will meet Fitchburg to understand it.
A fine tied to a restaurant's non-compliance was discussed as to who would be responsible after the business changed.

transfers.description: Transfer to capital reserve from retained earnings

decisions.decision: Legal costs stay under the town for now, with a working group to develop strategies for future funding and a policy on using counsel.
Business manager and town manager to agree on key numbers for the budget presentation; commission to tie them down at its next meeting.
Office space charge left at the current amount for this year, to be reviewed for next year's budget.
Engineering line to be raised to cover capital, service area and maintenance planning studies.
Fact-finding meeting to be sought with Fitchburg on CSS cost basis, early evening if possible.
Add a communications workshop and use of legal to a future agenda.

what_happened.line: The commission approved a sewer credit for a resident whose water leak raised her usage, calculated by the business manager under policy.
The commission voted to look at whether the Tilton Ave area qualifies for the sewer service area.
Legal costs stay under the town for now; a working group will develop future funding strategies and a policy on using counsel.
The FY19 sewer budget was not finished: the capital reserve transfer was left unresolved and the bottom line left in deficit.
The commission voted to send the restitution agreement draft for signature; the office space charge stays as is this year, to be reviewed for next year.

why_it_matters: Sewer bills fund the enterprise budget, so unsettled legal, indirect-cost and capital reserve lines could affect sewer rates and what the town budget, mostly taxes, is asked to carry.
The Tilton Ave review could decide whether homes on that street with failing septic systems can connect to the public sewer, and who would pay for the extension.
watch_next: The commission's next meeting, where it is to tie down key budget numbers with the town manager ahead of the Finance Committee presentation.
A fact-finding meeting with Fitchburg on the cost basis for CSS charges, which the commission said it would seek.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the credit, Tilton Ave., restitution agreement and privilege fee votes, and on most discussion topics. The main differences are that the official minutes list no vote on the office space charge, and that several of our figures are caption garble. The official minutes also give legal at $5000 where ours says costs stay under the town, and our capital reserve transfer does not appear in the official minutes.
